Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You have my claim number.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Pearland, Texas, turning left at an intersection with a traffic light. I was heading toward a shopping center.
Q: Walk me through what you were doing right before impact.
A: The light was green for me, or it had just turned yellow. I was waiting to turn left, and when there was a gap in the
oncoming traffic I started my turn.
Q: What did you see from the other vehicle?
A: A pickup truck came through from the opposite direction. I didn't see it until it was almost on top of me. I braked,
but it hit the front driver's side of my car.
Q: Did you have your seatbelt on?
A: Yes, I always do.
Q: Were you able to get out of the car on your own?
A: Yes, but my right knee was hurting rihgt away. I could barely put weight on it.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same day, and they sent me for imaging. They said there may be a torn ligament,
and I've been referred to an orthopedic specialist.
Q: Are you still having trouble with the knee?
A: Yes. Stairs are difficult, and it swells up by the evening. I've been using a brace and crutches for part of the week.
Q: Did you miss any time from work?
A: I have been out for about a week and a half. My job involves a lot of standing, so I've been working modified hours
since then.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was following the rules of the road, and I want this resolved so I can get my knee treated.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
